nodes.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$, let $(p_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of natural numbers with $p_k \le d$ for all $k$, and let $n$ be the largest value occurring infinitely often in $(p_k)$. Then $p_k \le n$ for all sufficiently large $k$.
nodes.title: The tail of a bounded sequence is bounded by its largest infinitely occurring value

nodes.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$. If a sequence $(p_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ of natural numbers satisfies $p_k \le d$ for all $k$, then some natural number $n \le d$ is the largest value occurring infinitely often in $(p_k)$.
nodes.title: Bounded sequences have a largest infinitely occurring value

nodes.summary: Let $(p_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of natural numbers and let $j, n \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $n$ is the largest value occurring infinitely often in the shifted sequence $(p_{j+k})_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ if and only if $n$ is the largest value occurring infinitely often in $(p_k)$.
nodes.title: Prefix independence of the largest infinitely occurring value

nodes.summary: Let $(p_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of natural numbers and $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $n$ is the largest value occurring infinitely often in $(p_k)$ if $p_k = n$ for infinitely many $k$, and every $m \in \mathbb{N}$ with $p_k = m$ for infinitely many $k$ satisfies $m \le n$.
nodes.title: Largest infinitely occurring value

nodes.summary: Let $(p_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of natural numbers with $p_k \in \{1, 2\}$ for every $k$. Then $(p_k)$ satisfies the even max-parity condition if and only if $p_k = 2$ for infinitely many $k$.
nodes.title: Max-parity with priorities 1 and 2 is the Büchi condition

nodes.summary: A sequence $(p_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ of natural numbers (priorities) satisfies the even max-parity condition if there is an even $n$ that is the largest value occurring infinitely often in $(p_k)$.
nodes.title: Even max-parity condition

nodes.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$. If a sequence $(p_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ of natural numbers satisfies $p_k \le d$ for all $k$, then it satisfies the odd max-parity condition if and only if it does not satisfy the even max-parity condition.
nodes.title: For bounded sequences the odd parity condition is the negation of the even one

nodes.summary: A sequence $(p_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ of natural numbers (priorities) satisfies the odd max-parity condition if there is an odd $n$ that is the largest value occurring infinitely often in $(p_k)$.
nodes.title: Odd max-parity condition
